rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the file; this lecture is definitional/framing prose (what a skill is, borrowed vs. authored judgement, the proportion, trust artifacts, the tool-flags-you-decide close) with no live-demo beat to break.

Chunk 0 is the H1-only title slide, exempt by convention. Every ##-chunk (1-6) carries 2-4 bullets each landing a self-carrying claim (definition, the borrowed/own split, the personal-to-team path, the proportion + principle, the three trust artifacts, the tool-flags-you-decide close). None is a bare wait-state.

Checked all 6 headers against their post-lean-pass content: "What a skill is" (ch1, defines the term), "Borrowed judgement, or your own" (ch2, security-practitioner vs. you bullets), "Your authored skill starts personal, then compounds" (ch3, personal path then team-kit growth), "Two curated, one authored" (ch4, the proportion + principle), "Three trust artifacts the next engineer checks" (ch5, names the three artifacts, checked by the next engineer), "The tool flags; you make the call" (ch6, access-control/STRIDE flag, student decides, closes "Go."). No header contradicted by its chunk's content after the cuts.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction (chunk 5 line 30's "Not 'we followed a checklist' but: whoever touches this feature next can see the reasoning and check it against the code" is a single negation+contrast, not the banned two-negation triple). Closest anaphora candidate: chunk 6 line 34, "What it got right, what it underweighted, what it missed that you know matters" — third leg carries new concrete content (the student's own knowledge check), so it stays inside the pair-or-earn-the-third-leg test. Grepped for self-grading superlatives ("most useful", "best", "one of the") — none present. No number-with-retraction (line 17's "153 contributors, 31% ... by the company's own count" is a number with its label, not a hedge-then-retract). No abstraction-noun stacks; no empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exactly two bolded spans in the whole file: chunk 1 line 5, **skill** (single-word handle at its definition) and chunk 4 line 24, **Don't make general what you don't practice yourself.** (an 8-word clause, over the stated ≲5-word cap read literally). The maintainer block's dated Emphasis pass note (line 44, 2026-07-09, Antti-directed "go very lightly on the bold") names this exact pair as the two handles the file was deliberately reduced to, and no other slide carries any bold. Harm rule 9 exists to prevent (bold-monoculture, every bullet opening bold) is absent: budget is ≤1 bolded element per slide on both slides that carry any, and the principle line is the module's coined governing law, the shape the rule itself treats as a handle even when long. Re-flagging a dated, maintainer-attested, previously-audited choice on word count alone is the "obvious fix would degrade a deliberate artefact" case the dispatch preamble tells judges to surface as a rule question rather than a REVISE — and this exact question was already surfaced and settled on 2026-07-09.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings should be claims per rule 15, but two remain noun-phrase topic labels with no verb/assertion: chunk 1 line 3 "What a skill is" (a definitional label) and chunk 4 line 19 "Two curated, one authored" (a ratio label). Neither fits the stated NOT-violation carve-outs (orientation headers, catalogue entries naming their subject, phase/section labels inside a walk). By contrast chunk 3 line 14 ("Your authored skill starts personal, then compounds") and chunk 6 line 32 ("The tool flags; you make the call") are genuine subject+verb claims, and chunk 5 line 26 ("Three trust artifacts the next engineer checks") carries enough of a relative-clause assertion to pass. Harm check, applying the template's own classification principle (rules 15-16 postdate the template's blocking/non-blocking list and must self-classify): the failure mode here is register/mood, not comprehension — a reader is not confused by "What a skill is", only the slide's mood is a beat flatter than a declared law would be. That is "this could be tighter", not "I cannot follow this", and matches the compendium's own documented history for this rule ("a rule that only ever produces notes is a rule mis-scoped") and Antti's own carve-out elsewhere on this rule ("not every header owes a claim"). Non-blocking.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the maintainer wants strict conformance: recast as claims, e.g. "A skill is judgement someone else already packaged" / "Two proportions, and only one of them you can author" — otherwise leave as labels; this rule's own history treats that as acceptable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file already received a same-day, Antti-directed lean pass (2026-08-25, same date as this rule's own compounded entry) that cut exactly this class: (b) self-referential design commentary ("It arrived unpackaged because skills hadn't yet been introduced as a primitive.") and a padding lead ("Your skills folder, starting today."), plus a kicker and a duplicate bullet, per the maintainer block's own dated note (line 42). Closest remaining candidate: chunk 4 line 24's trailing sentence, "The curated skills come from people who did the work; the one you author covers what only you do" — a near-restatement of the split chunk 2 already established. Judged as earning its slot, not cut: it is the sentence that DEFINES the module's newly-coined bolded principle ("Don't make general what you don't practice yourself") in concrete terms, it was written/kept the same day this rule was authored (maintainer had "free hands" and chose to keep it), and cutting it would leave the bolded law undefined at its one appearance. "Go." (chunk 6 close) is not an aphorism-kicker restating the header — it is a bare 2-word transition to the exercises, adding nothing to cut because it asserts nothing. Chunk 5's closer (line 30) adds a concrete criterion ("can see the reasoning and check it against the code") beyond its header, so it earns its slot rather than merely restating it.
